title: Architecture and trust boundaries documented
standard_refs: NIST SSDF PO.1|NIST AI RMF MAP 1|OWASP Top 10:2021 A04
requirement: Document trust boundaries, sensitive data flows, privileged components, external providers and production attack surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
A current diagram/inventory lists every runtime component, data store, external provider and trust boundary.
Each sensitive data flow names its source, destination and protection.
The inventory was reviewed after the last material architecture change.
verification_steps:
Compare the inventory with deployed services, environment variables and provider dashboards.
Trace one sensitive record from intake to deletion and confirm every hop is documented.
test_method: Review current architecture/data-flow documentation against deployed components.
evidence_expected: Current data-flow/trust-boundary diagram and component inventory.
remediation_guidance: Write a one-page data-flow/trust-boundary map and add it to the release checklist so it changes with the architecture.

title: Sensitive data classification and lifecycle
standard_refs: NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy|GDPR Art. 5(1)(c),(e)|COPPA 16 CFR 312.10
requirement: Classify sensitive data and define collection, access, provider sharing, retention, deletion, logging and export rules.
acceptance_criteria:
Every stored data category has a classification, purpose, retention period and deletion mechanism.
Data sent to each external provider is listed with its retention terms.
Retention periods are enforced by code or scheduled jobs, not policy text alone.
verification_steps:
List tables, buckets, indexes, logs and provider copies; check each against the classification register.
Confirm a scheduled job or trigger enforces each retention period.
test_method: Trace representative records from collection through deletion and backups/providers.
evidence_expected: Data inventory, retention/deletion tests, vendor flow documentation.
remediation_guidance: Create a data register (category, location, purpose, retention, deletion path, providers) and implement retention jobs for anything without one.

title: Security release gate
requirement: Define security conditions that block public release and require explicit accepted-risk ownership.
acceptance_criteria:
A release cannot ship with an open P0 or an open release-blocker control without recorded accepted risk.
The gate report is regenerated from current evidence for each release.
verification_steps: Check the release process for a step that runs the readiness report and reads its decision.
test_method: Inspect release process and verify blockers cannot silently pass.
evidence_expected: Release gate document and CI/release evidence.
remediation_guidance: Run `security-readiness validate` and `report` in CI and require the gate decision in release sign-off.

title: Authentication required for private resources
requirement: Private resources and state-changing APIs require a valid authenticated principal.
acceptance_criteria:
Every private page, API route, server action and RPC rejects unauthenticated callers.
Guest/anonymous sessions cannot reach private or paid operations unless the product explicitly intends it.
Each private endpoint has an automated unauthenticated negative test.
verification_steps:
Generate a route inventory and call each private route with no credentials, an expired token and a malformed token.
Call the data layer directly (e.g. PostgREST/Storage with the public key) without a session.
test_method: Attempt unauthenticated access to every private route/API.
evidence_expected: Route tests plus auth middleware/server checks.
remediation_guidance: Centralize auth in one helper per surface (page, route, action), reject anonymous sessions there, and add an inventory-driven negative test.

title: OAuth state, PKCE and redirect safety
requirement: OAuth uses state/PKCE protections and redirect destinations cannot become open redirects.
acceptance_criteria:
OAuth uses PKCE and state validation.
Post-login redirects accept only same-origin relative paths.
Redirect allowlists in the identity provider contain no broad wildcards.
verification_steps:
Attempt login with next=//evil.example, next=https://evil.example and encoded variants.
Review provider redirect URL allowlists for production and preview.
test_method: Test forged callback, malformed state, external/encoded redirect targets and preview/prod allowlists.
evidence_expected: Callback validation code and integration tests.
remediation_guidance: Use the provider SDK's PKCE flow, validate `next` with a same-origin path parser, and pin redirect URLs per environment.

title: Session lifecycle and logout
requirement: Sessions expire, refresh and terminate predictably; logout invalidates usable sessions.
acceptance_criteria:
Logout invalidates the server-side session/refresh token.
Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.
Expired sessions cannot call private APIs.
verification_steps:
Log out, replay the old cookie/refresh token against a private API.
Inspect Set-Cookie attributes in production.
test_method: Test expiration, rotation/refresh, logout, multi-tab behavior and stolen/old session reuse.
evidence_expected: Session configuration and browser/API tests.
remediation_guidance: Use the identity provider's server-side sign-out and the framework's supported cookie session pattern.

title: Account creation and credential abuse protections
frameworks: OWASP API Security Top 10|OWASP Top 10|OWASP ASVS 5.0
requirement: Public sign-up, guest and anonymous accounts cannot be created or used at a scale that multiplies cost or abuse; credentials resist stuffing and breached passwords.
acceptance_criteria:
Anonymous/guest sign-in is disabled, or guest accounts are limited by policy, quota and cleanup.
CAPTCHA or equivalent bot protection guards sign-up and sign-in.
Breached-password checks and a minimum length are enforced by the identity provider, not only the UI.
Auth endpoints are rate-limited.
verification_steps:
Script 50 sign-ups from one IP and from rotating IPs.
Call the identity provider's sign-up API directly with a weak/breached password.
Count anonymous accounts in production.
test_method: Review identity-provider settings and attempt scripted account creation and credential stuffing.
evidence_expected: Provider settings export/screenshots and scripted-abuse test results.
remediation_guidance: Disable anonymous sign-in (or bound it), enable CAPTCHA, breached-password protection and auth rate limits, and treat guest sessions as signed out for paid operations.

title: Privileged and admin access protected
requirement: Admin/operator capabilities require a separate role checked server-side, MFA, and produce an audit trail.
acceptance_criteria:
Every admin function checks an admin role on the server.
Admin accounts require MFA.
Admin actions are logged immutably with actor and target.
verification_steps:
Call each admin endpoint as a normal user.
Sign in as an admin without MFA.
test_method: Attempt admin functions as a normal user; review MFA enforcement and audit logs.
evidence_expected: Role checks in code, MFA policy, audit log samples.
remediation_guidance: Add a server-side role check helper, enforce MFA for admin roles and write admin actions to an append-only log.

title: Object-level authorization / tenant isolation
requirement: A principal cannot read, mutate, delete, infer or retrieve another tenant/user's objects by substituting IDs.
acceptance_criteria:
Every object ID accepted from a client (path, query, body) is authorized against the caller, not just validated.
Tenant isolation is enforced in the data layer (e.g. RLS) and tested with two real users.
Substituting another tenant's ID returns not-found or forbidden on every route.
verification_steps:
For each route taking an ID, call it as user B with user A's ID.
Run database-level tests that execute policies as two different users.
test_method: Systematically substitute foreign IDs across every object API and retrieval path.
evidence_expected: RLS/IAM policies and negative authorization tests.
remediation_guidance: Enforce ownership in the database (RLS or equivalent) and check it in the route before any privileged write.

title: Privileged/service-role operations scoped
requirement: Every privileged operation that bypasses row-level controls independently proves user, tenant and object scope.
acceptance_criteria:
Every use of a privileged (RLS-bypassing/service) credential is listed.
Each privileged call is preceded by an ownership check under the caller's identity and passes the owner explicitly.
Privileged credentials never reach client bundles.
verification_steps:
Search the codebase for the privileged client constructor and review every call site.
Search built client bundles for the privileged key name/value.
test_method: Inventory privileged clients/RPCs; verify precondition and owner filters; run forged-ID tests.
evidence_expected: Privileged-call inventory plus owner-scope tests.
remediation_guidance: Wrap the privileged client in a server-only module and make owner/tenant a required argument of every privileged function.

title: Auxiliary/internal services authenticated
requirement: Internal/auxiliary services are either network-isolated or authenticate callers and authorize object scope.
acceptance_criteria:
Every auxiliary service either listens only on a private/loopback network or authenticates callers.
Auxiliary services authorize the tenant/owner of every request, not just the caller service.
verification_steps:
List every deployed service, port and ingress rule.
Call each auxiliary service without credentials and with another tenant's identifiers.
test_method: Attempt direct requests without service identity and with foreign resource identifiers.
evidence_expected: Network/IAM configuration and service auth tests.
remediation_guidance: Put auxiliary services on a private network and require a signed service token that carries the end-user/tenant identity.

title: Server-side input validation and bounds
requirement: API inputs are type/length/range/enum validated server-side before privileged work.
acceptance_criteria:
Every route validates type, format (e.g. UUID), length and enum of each input before use.
Invalid input returns 4xx, never 500.
Mass assignment is impossible: writes use explicit field lists.
verification_steps:
Fuzz each route with wrong types, oversized strings and unknown fields.
Review writes for spread/passthrough of client objects.
test_method: Fuzz malformed, oversized, duplicate, null and boundary values.
evidence_expected: Validation code and API tests.
remediation_guidance: Add a shared request schema validator and use it at the top of every route.

title: Rate, concurrency and cost limits
frameworks: OWASP API Security|OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10
requirement: Public expensive operations have per-principal/IP rate limits, concurrency bounds, token/work limits and global spend/circuit breakers.
acceptance_criteria:
Expensive routes have per-user and per-IP rate limits enforced at the edge and in the app.
Model calls set output-token caps and timeouts; retries are bounded.
Per-user daily budgets and a global spend ceiling/circuit breaker exist.
Reprocessing/regeneration paths cannot loop without limit.
verification_steps:
Burst each expensive route and confirm 429s before cost accrues.
Check every provider call for max output tokens and timeout.
Confirm provider-side budget alerts and hard limits.
test_method: Burst and sustained abuse tests; verify limit behavior and no unbounded provider spend.
evidence_expected: Limiter configuration, spend guardrails and load/abuse tests.
remediation_guidance: Add edge rate-limit rules (log mode first), a per-user usage table checked before provider calls, output-token caps, and provider budget alerts.

title: CSRF / request provenance protection
standard_refs: OWASP Top 10:2021 A01|OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Web Frontend Security)
requirement: Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests validate same-origin/request provenance or an equivalent anti-CSRF mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
State-changing requests with cookie auth are protected by SameSite cookies plus origin checks or CSRF tokens.
GET requests never change state.
verification_steps: Submit a cross-site form/fetch to each mutating route with a valid session cookie.
test_method: Submit state-changing requests cross-site with a valid victim session.
evidence_expected: Origin/CSRF middleware and negative browser tests.
remediation_guidance: Rely on framework CSRF protection (e.g. server actions' origin check) and add Origin validation to custom mutating routes.

title: Production errors do not disclose internals
requirement: Client responses use generic errors/trace IDs while internal details stay in protected logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Clients receive fixed messages; database, provider and stack details stay in server logs.
Streamed/async error channels follow the same rule.
verification_steps: Trigger DB constraint, provider and unexpected errors on each route and inspect responses.
test_method: Force DB/provider/parser failures and inspect client responses.
evidence_expected: Central error boundary and tests.
remediation_guidance: Add one error mapper that returns a fixed message plus a request ID and logs the detail server-side.

title: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) protections
frameworks: OWASP API Security Top 10|OWASP Top 10|OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10
requirement: Requests to user-, document- or model-influenced destinations cannot reach internal networks, metadata endpoints or unintended hosts.
acceptance_criteria:
Destinations are allowlisted or resolved and checked against private/link-local ranges after DNS resolution.
Redirects are re-validated.
Responses are size- and time-bounded.
verification_steps: Request http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost, an internal hostname and a redirect to them.
test_method: Supply internal, metadata, redirecting and DNS-rebinding URLs to every fetching feature.
evidence_expected: Egress allowlist/validation code and SSRF test results.
remediation_guidance: Route outbound fetches through one guarded client with an allowlist, post-resolution IP checks and redirect re-validation.

title: Inbound webhook authenticity and replay protection
requirement: Webhook endpoints verify the sender's signature, reject replays and are idempotent.
acceptance_criteria:
Every webhook verifies an HMAC/signature over the raw body with a constant-time compare.
Timestamps outside a tolerance window are rejected.
Processing is idempotent by event ID.
verification_steps: Replay a captured event; send a modified body with the original signature.
test_method: Send unsigned, mis-signed, stale and duplicated webhook payloads.
evidence_expected: Signature verification code and negative tests.
remediation_guidance: Use the provider's signature verification helper on the raw body and store processed event IDs.

title: Browser security headers / CSP
standard_refs: OWASP Top 10:2021 A05|OWASP CSP Cheat Sheet
requirement: Production sends an appropriate CSP and modern browser hardening headers.
acceptance_criteria:
Production responses send CSP (at least frame-ancestors, base-uri, object-src), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and HSTS.
A full CSP is enforced, or is in Report-Only with a dated plan to enforce.
verification_steps:
curl -I the production domain and key routes; compare headers to the policy.
Load the app with the Report-Only policy and review violations.
test_method: Inspect deployed headers and test framing/script/connect behavior.
evidence_expected: Header configuration and deployment test.
remediation_guidance: Set headers centrally (framework config or edge), ship the full CSP as Report-Only, then enforce after a browser pass.

title: Untrusted/model output rendered safely
requirement: Untrusted and model-generated content cannot become executable HTML/JS/URLs without validation/sanitization.
acceptance_criteria:
Model output and user content are rendered as text/structured nodes, never raw HTML.
Links and images in untrusted content are disabled or sanitized.
An XSS payload regression test exists.
verification_steps: Render , javascript: links and markdown-embedded HTML through every display path.
test_method: Inject HTML, script, javascript URLs, image beacons and malicious Markdown through user/source/model paths.
evidence_expected: Safe renderer implementation and XSS/output-handling tests.
remediation_guidance: Render through a parser that emits framework nodes only; add payload fixtures to tests.

title: Upload allowlist, size and filename controls
standard_refs: OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet|OWASP API4:2023
requirement: Uploads use allowed types, bounded size, generated/scoped storage names and safe filenames.
acceptance_criteria:
Only allowlisted types and extensions are accepted.
Size limits are enforced server-side and at the storage layer.
Stored names are server-generated; original names are display-only.
verification_steps: Upload a disallowed extension, an oversized file and a path-traversal filename.
test_method: Upload forbidden extensions/types, empty/oversized files and hostile filenames.
evidence_expected: Upload policy and tests.
remediation_guidance: Enforce an allowlist and size in the route and in storage-bucket configuration; generate storage keys server-side.

title: Content signature and parser validation
requirement: Server validates actual file content/signature/parser compatibility rather than trusting extension or Content-Type.
acceptance_criteria:
The bytes of every upload are checked against the accepted type (magic bytes / structure).
A renamed or polyglot file is rejected before storage or parsing.
verification_steps: Upload HTML renamed to .pdf, an executable renamed to .png and a PDF/HTML polyglot.
test_method: Rename executables/archives/polyglots as allowed formats; send mismatched MIME and corrupt files.
evidence_expected: Magic-byte/parser validation plus adversarial fixtures.
remediation_guidance: Check signatures for each allowed format before storage; serve originals with forced download and nosniff.

title: Archive/decompression/image/OCR resource bounds
standard_refs: OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet|OWASP API4:2023
requirement: Compressed/container formats and images are bounded by expanded size, entry count, dimensions/pages and downstream work.
acceptance_criteria:
Archive-based formats are bounded by entry count, expanded size and ratio before inflation.
Image dimensions, page counts and OCR pages are capped.
Parsers run with time and memory budgets.
verification_steps: Upload a zip bomb disguised as DOCX, a 30k×30k PNG and a 5,000-page PDF.
test_method: Zip/OOXML bombs, huge dimensions, excessive pages and pathological parser inputs.
evidence_expected: Pre-extraction limits and resource-abuse tests.
remediation_guidance: Inspect archive directories before parsing, cap pixels/pages, and run parsing in a worker with resource limits.

title: Malware/quarantine controls
requirement: Untrusted files are quarantined/scanned or otherwise prevented from being redistributed/processed beyond the accepted risk model.
acceptance_criteria:
Uploads are scanned or disarmed before they are processed or served to anyone.
Unscanned or flagged files stay quarantined.
verification_steps: Upload the EICAR test file and confirm it is quarantined.
test_method: Use safe anti-malware test fixture and verify quarantine/rejection path.
evidence_expected: Scanner/quarantine integration and tests.
remediation_guidance: Add scanning (e.g. ClamAV in the ingestion worker or a scanning service) and a quarantined status.

title: Private storage and scoped download
standard_refs: OWASP API1:2023|OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet
requirement: Original files are private; download links are authorization-gated and short-lived.
acceptance_criteria:
Buckets holding user files are private.
Downloads use short-lived signed URLs issued after an ownership check.
Storage policies prevent listing or writing another owner's path.
verification_steps:
Request another user's object path directly and via the download route.
Check bucket public flags in the provider dashboard.
test_method: Attempt foreign-file download and expired/replayed signed URLs.
evidence_expected: Storage policy, signed URL implementation and tests.
remediation_guidance: Keep buckets private, scope storage policies by owner prefix, and issue signed URLs of 5 minutes or less.

title: Payment processing delegated and verified server-side
standard_refs: PCI DSS v4.0 (SAQ A scope)|OWASP API6:2023
frameworks: PCI DSS v4.0|OWASP API Security Top 10
requirement: Card data is handled only by a PCI-compliant provider's hosted fields/checkout; prices and entitlements are computed and granted server-side from verified provider events.
acceptance_criteria:
No card numbers touch application servers or logs.
Prices come from server-side configuration, not the client.
Entitlements are granted only from verified provider events.
verification_steps:
Change the price/plan ID in the checkout request.
Grant an entitlement by calling the success URL without paying.
test_method: Tamper with client-side price/plan parameters and confirm fulfillment only follows verified events.
evidence_expected: Hosted checkout integration, server-side price lookup, webhook-driven fulfillment.
remediation_guidance: Use hosted checkout, look up prices server-side and fulfill only from signed webhooks.

title: Uploaded/retrieved content treated as untrusted
standard_refs: OWASP LLM01:2025|OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
frameworks: OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10|NIST AI RMF
requirement: User/source content cannot redefine trusted system policy or tool authority.
acceptance_criteria:
Retrieved/uploaded content and anything derived from it (titles, metadata, earlier model output) reaches prompts only inside a delimited untrusted-data envelope.
No browser-supplied text is placed in system/developer instructions.
Prompts state that untrusted data cannot change instructions.
verification_steps:
Trace every string that enters a system prompt back to its origin.
Inject instructions via document body, filename, metadata and OCR text and inspect the assembled prompt.
test_method: Embed policy-override instructions in text, document metadata, OCR images and retrieved passages.
evidence_expected: Prompt/data boundary plus adversarial tests.
remediation_guidance: Serialize untrusted data (e.g. JSON envelope), keep it out of system text, and build scope/context directives server-side.

title: Prompt-injection regression suite
requirement: Direct/indirect prompt injection is tested through actual production model boundaries and cannot cause unauthorized data/tool/state changes.
acceptance_criteria:
A versioned corpus of direct and indirect injection cases runs against the production prompt path and model.
Results are reviewed and regressions block release.
verification_steps: Run the corpus against the deployed configuration and record pass/fail per case.
test_method: Run maintained adversarial corpus through renderer/evaluator/tool boundaries.
evidence_expected: Versioned adversarial eval results.
remediation_guidance: Add injection fixtures to the evaluation suite and run them on every prompt/model change.

title: Structured validation for machine-affecting model output
requirement: Model output that affects software state is schema-validated and range/enum checked.
acceptance_criteria:
Model output that drives state (grades, IDs, actions) is parsed against a strict schema and normalized.
Invalid output fails closed.
verification_steps: Feed malformed/extra-field model output into each parser.
test_method: Force malformed/extra/invalid model fields and verify fail-closed normalization.
evidence_expected: Schemas/normalizers and tests.
remediation_guidance: Use strict structured outputs and validate again server-side before use.

title: Least privilege for tools and autonomous actions
frameworks: OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10|NIST AI RMF
requirement: Models cannot invoke tools or mutate privileged state beyond explicitly authorized, scoped operations.
acceptance_criteria:
Each tool has the minimum scope and runs with the end user's permissions.
Destructive or external actions need human confirmation.
Tool calls are logged.
verification_steps: Prompt-inject a tool call that exceeds the user's permissions.
test_method: Prompt model to call unauthorized tools, expand scope or alter authority.
evidence_expected: Tool allowlists, authorization checks and adversarial tests.
remediation_guidance: Scope tools per user, require confirmation for side effects, and log every invocation.

title: Sensitive-data disclosure testing
requirement: Model/context paths cannot reveal secrets, system credentials, private prompts or another user's data.
acceptance_criteria:
Tests show the model cannot reveal another tenant's data, secrets or system prompt contents that matter.
Prompts contain no secrets.
verification_steps: With two tenants' data present, ask for the other tenant's content via chat and retrieval.
test_method: Exfiltration prompts, cross-tenant prompts, system-prompt extraction and context-boundary tests.
evidence_expected: Adversarial eval and isolation tests.
remediation_guidance: Scope retrieval by tenant in the data layer and add cross-tenant decoys to evaluations.

title: Model, prompt and evaluator version traceability
standard_refs: NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2|NIST AI 600-1: Information Integrity
requirement: AI decisions can be tied to model, prompt, embedding/retrieval and evaluator versions.
acceptance_criteria: Every stored AI output records model, prompt version and retrieval/evaluator version.
verification_steps: Pick a stored answer and identify the exact model and prompt that produced it.
test_method: Inspect persisted traces/evidence for version identifiers and reproduce a sampled decision.
evidence_expected: Versioned configs/traces and reproducibility test.
remediation_guidance: Version prompts in code and store model/prompt IDs with outputs.

title: AI latency/token/cost observability
frameworks: NIST AI RMF|OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10
requirement: AI operations expose bounded latency, token/work usage and cost metrics without logging raw sensitive content by default.
acceptance_criteria:
Tokens, latency, cost and errors are recorded per operation and user.
Alerts fire on spend or error anomalies.
verification_steps: Find yesterday's cost by operation and the top-spending user.
test_method: Exercise each AI operation and verify traces, limits and dashboard metrics.
evidence_expected: Telemetry schema/dashboard/query evidence.
remediation_guidance: Log usage from provider responses to a metrics store and add spend/error alerts.

title: Content safety appropriate to the user population
standard_refs: NIST AI 600-1: Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content|NIST AI 600-1: Obscene, Degrading, and/or Abusive Content|OWASP LLM05:2025
requirement: User input and generated or shared content are screened for harmful categories appropriate to the audience, with a safe response path for crisis content.
acceptance_criteria:
Learner/user input and model or user-generated output pass a moderation check before display.
Self-harm content routes to a safe-messaging response with resources.
Moderation decisions are logged without content.
verification_steps: Submit each corpus category through chat, uploads and shared content.
test_method: Run a harmful-content corpus (self-harm, sexual content, violence, harassment) through every input and output path.
evidence_expected: Moderation calls in code, safe-messaging responses, test results.
remediation_guidance: Add a moderation step on input and output with category thresholds set for the audience and a crisis-response template.

title: Permission-preserving retrieval
frameworks: OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10|OWASP API Security
requirement: Retrieval enforces tenant/user/source permissions before content enters model context.
acceptance_criteria:
Vector search filters by tenant inside the data layer under the caller's identity.
Callers cannot widen scope through parameters.
verification_steps: Query retrieval as user B with user A's room/tenant ID and with forged owner parameters.
test_method: Use cross-tenant decoys and forged room/source IDs in retrieval.
evidence_expected: RLS/IAM retrieval path and adversarial eval.
remediation_guidance: Enforce tenant filters in the search function with security-invoker/RLS; ignore owner parameters from non-privileged callers.

title: Grounding, citation support and abstention verified
frameworks: OWASP GenAI / LLM Top 10|NIST AI RMF
requirement: Unsupported questions reliably abstain and cited claims are semantically supported, not merely syntactically cited.
acceptance_criteria:
A human-reviewed evaluation measures citation support and abstention on a frozen corpus.
Thresholds are defined and met for release.
verification_steps: Run the reviewed evaluation on the release candidate.
test_method: Human-reviewed corpus with claim-level support and unsupported-answer cases.
evidence_expected: Reviewed RAG scorecard and release thresholds.
remediation_guidance: Build a reviewed scorecard and gate prompt/retrieval changes on it.

title: Deletion and revision propagate to derived/vector data
requirement: Deleted/replaced source content cannot remain retrievable through stale chunks, indexes or caches.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting or revising a source removes or replaces its chunks, embeddings and every derived copy, including secondary indexes.
verification_steps: Delete a source and query every index and cache for its content.
test_method: Replace/delete source and query for removed content across every retrieval system.
evidence_expected: Deletion/revision implementation and stale-source regression tests.
remediation_guidance: Cascade deletes to derived data and add a deletion test per index.

title: Retention, deletion and export are implemented
requirement: User data has explicit retention/deletion/export behavior across primary, derived, cache/index and provider copies.
acceptance_criteria:
Users can delete their account and all derived data, including storage and provider copies where possible.
Users can export their data.
Retention jobs run on schedule.
verification_steps: Delete a test account and search every store for its identifiers.
test_method: Create representative data then exercise deletion/export and verify downstream artifacts.
evidence_expected: Policy plus end-to-end deletion/export tests.
remediation_guidance: Implement account deletion/export flows and retention jobs from the data register.

title: Minor/student-data release requirements resolved
standard_refs: COPPA 16 CFR Part 312|FERPA 34 CFR Part 99|NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy
requirement: Before public child use, identity/guardian/consent/collection/retention/vendor handling requirements are explicitly resolved for target markets.
acceptance_criteria:
Counsel has decided the audience (13+ screen or full COPPA compliance) and the decision is implemented.
If under-13 users are allowed: verifiable parental consent, separate consent for third-party disclosure, a written security program and a retention limit exist.
If schools are customers: contracts meet FERPA school-official criteria.
verification_steps:
Walk sign-up as an under-13 user.
Review consent records and the written security program.
test_method: Privacy/legal/product review against actual onboarding and data collection.
evidence_expected: Approved data/consent model and implementation evidence.
remediation_guidance: Get a counsel decision on audience; implement an age screen or the COPPA consent flow; document the security program.

title: External provider data flows documented and configured
standard_refs: OWASP LLM02:2025|NIST AI 600-1: Value Chain and Component Integration|GDPR Art. 28
requirement: Document what data each provider receives, retention/training settings, region/subprocessors where relevant, and deletion/incident expectations.
acceptance_criteria:
Each provider receiving user data is listed with data types, retention, training use and a signed DPA.
Provider settings (e.g. response storage, retention) match the register.
verification_steps: Compare the register with code call sites and provider dashboards.
test_method: Compare provider configuration/contracts against actual request payloads.
evidence_expected: Vendor data-flow register and configuration evidence.
remediation_guidance: Create a vendor register, sign DPAs, and set provider retention/training controls (e.g. store:false).

title: Privacy notice, terms and data-subject requests
requirement: A privacy notice, terms of service and a working channel for access/deletion requests are published and match actual data handling.
acceptance_criteria:
Privacy notice and terms are linked from sign-up and the app.
The notice lists every provider receiving user data.
Access and deletion requests can be submitted and are fulfilled within the stated period.
verification_steps:
Read the notice against the vendor register.
Submit a test deletion request.
test_method: Compare published notices with the data register and test the request channel.
evidence_expected: Published URLs, data register, request-handling log.
remediation_guidance: Draft notice/terms with counsel from the data register and link them from sign-up; add a request form or address.

title: Security-relevant events are observable
standard_refs: OWASP Top 10:2021 A09|OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet
requirement: Detect auth failures, authorization denials, suspicious abuse, privileged failures, upload/malware failures and relevant AI-security events.
acceptance_criteria:
Auth failures, authorization denials, rate-limit hits and admin actions are logged with request IDs.
Alerts exist for spikes.
verification_steps: Trigger each event and find it in the log/alert system.
test_method: Trigger representative events and confirm protected, searchable records/alerts.
evidence_expected: Security event schema, logs and alert tests.
remediation_guidance: Emit structured security events and route them to alerting.

title: Logs avoid sensitive-content leakage
requirement: Logs/telemetry do not routinely store secrets, session tokens, full private documents or raw learner content without explicit necessity/protection.
acceptance_criteria: Logs and telemetry contain no document content, learner answers, tokens or secrets.
verification_steps: Sample production logs and telemetry for content and credentials.
test_method: Inspect production logging/telemetry payloads during auth, upload, AI and error flows.
evidence_expected: Logging policy and sampled traces.
remediation_guidance: Log codes and IDs only; add a redaction layer for anything else.

title: Reproducible dependency install and vulnerability scanning
standard_refs: OWASP LLM03:2025|OWASP Top 10:2021 A06|NIST SSDF PW.4|NIST SSDF RV.1
frameworks: NIST SSDF|OWASP Software Supply Chain guidance
requirement: CI uses committed dependency locks and automated vulnerability/SCA checks.
acceptance_criteria:
No floating version specifiers (e.g. latest) in manifests.
CI installs from the lockfile only.
CI fails on high/critical advisories in production dependencies.
Automated dependency security updates are enabled.
verification_steps: grep manifests for floating specifiers; read the CI install command; run the audit command.
test_method: Inspect CI install mode and intentionally verify vulnerable dependency reporting path.
evidence_expected: Frozen-lock install and SCA workflow.
remediation_guidance: Pin versions, use frozen-lockfile installs, add an audit gate and Dependabot/Renovate.

title: Secret scanning
frameworks: NIST SSDF|OWASP Software Supply Chain guidance
requirement: Repositories and CI detect committed credentials/secrets and define rotation response.
acceptance_criteria:
Secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repository.
No live secrets exist in history.
verification_steps: Check repository security settings; run a history scan.
test_method: Use safe fake-secret fixture or scanner test mode.
evidence_expected: Secret scanning workflow and rotation runbook.
remediation_guidance: Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection; rotate anything found.

title: SBOM / dependency inventory
frameworks: NIST SSDF|OWASP Software Supply Chain guidance
requirement: Production releases have a machine-readable dependency inventory/SBOM or equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Each release produces an SBOM/dependency inventory artifact.
verification_steps: Find the SBOM for the current production release.
test_method: Generate release inventory and confirm direct/transitive dependencies are represented.
evidence_expected: SBOM artifact or dependency inventory.
remediation_guidance: Generate an SBOM in CI (e.g. CycloneDX) and attach it to releases.

title: Protected production branch and required checks
requirement: Production branch changes require review/required checks and cannot silently bypass security validation.
acceptance_criteria:
The production branch is protected; direct pushes and force-pushes are blocked.
Required status checks include tests and the security gate.
verification_steps: Read branch protection rules for the production branch.
test_method: Inspect branch rules and attempt prohibited direct/broken change in a safe test repo/branch.
evidence_expected: Branch protection/ruleset and required-check configuration.
remediation_guidance: Enable branch protection with required checks and at least one review.

title: Security incident response and credential rotation
standard_refs: NIST SSDF RV.2|NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4
requirement: Document detection, containment, credential rotation, provider shutdown, user impact assessment and recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
A written runbook covers incident triage, user notification, and rotation of every credential.
Rotation of each secret has been rehearsed.
verification_steps: Rotate one production secret using only the runbook.
test_method: Tabletop one auth/data/AI-cost incident and record gaps.
evidence_expected: Incident runbook and tabletop record.
remediation_guidance: Write the runbook with a per-secret rotation table and rehearse it.

title: Backup/recovery and destructive-change validation
requirement: Critical data has defined backup/recovery behavior and destructive operations are tested against it.
acceptance_criteria:
Backups exist at the required frequency and a restore has been tested.
Restores respect deletion/retention (deleted data is not resurrected silently).
verification_steps: Restore to a scratch environment and verify integrity and deletions.
test_method: Restore representative state and verify deletion/retention semantics are not contradicted.
evidence_expected: Recovery test evidence.
remediation_guidance: Confirm the backup tier, schedule restore drills and document deletion handling after restore.

title: Hosting and managed-platform security configuration
standard_refs: OWASP Top 10:2021 A05|OWASP API8:2023|NIST SSDF PO.5
frameworks: OWASP Top 10|NIST SSDF|Supabase production checklist|Vercel security docs
requirement: Owner accounts, managed backends and hosting are configured for production: MFA, least-privilege team access, secret scoping, preview protection, TLS, platform security advisors clean.
acceptance_criteria:
All owner/admin accounts on hosting, database, AI and source platforms use MFA.
Platform security advisors report no unresolved warnings.
Secrets are marked sensitive and scoped to the environments that need them; preview deployments are protected and do not use production data unintentionally.
Database SSL enforcement, network restrictions, custom SMTP and backups are configured where offered.
verification_steps:
Walk each platform's production checklist and record each item.
Run the platform security advisor.
test_method: Review each platform's security settings and advisors against its production checklist.
evidence_expected: Settings exports/screenshots, advisor output, environment variable scoping.
remediation_guidance: Complete each platform's production checklist and re-run its advisor after changes.
